required_tuples.rationale: Auto-registration creates exactly one active user carrying the provider username, verified email and subject link, plus one refreshable session.
With auto-registration off an unknown subject, and a provider error, each answer 302 Unauthorized and create no user or session.
Broken-signature, foreign-issuer, foreign-audience and expired ID tokens are denied with the login redirect and create no user or session.

Auto-registration emits one user_added with the legacy user fields (id, username, email, type, token, isActive, hasOpenIDLink, permissions, arrays) to the root socket and none to an ordinary user socket.
An email-matched callback keeps the user's id, username, email, type and extraData members and adds only authOpenIDSub plus one session.
An explicitly unverified email is denied with the login redirect, links nothing and creates no session.
An absent email_verified claim is not false, so the email match links the existing user: id, username, email and type are kept, authOpenIDSub is added, one session exists and no user is created.

With email matching configured, a userinfo without an email is denied with the Unauthorized redirect even when a local user has the same username; nothing is linked, no session exists and the rows are unchanged.

A second subject whose email belongs to a user already linked to another sub is denied with Unauthorized; the original link and session are kept, the second subject stays unlinked and no user is added.

With MatchExistingBy=username, a mode the web client offers, preferred_username matching links the unlinked local user, keeps its id, username, email and type, adds authOpenIDSub and one session without creating a user.
Two web logins of one subject keep one user with the same id, add two refreshable sessions and emit no second user_added.

Native starts reject an unlisted URI and a missing challenge; a valid start's challenge and state appear in the provider URL and app link, the state is consumed once, and the callback still completes.
A web start sets the auth_cb/auth_method/session cookies; the callback sets refresh and openid_id_token cookies and an access token whose userId, username and type identify the linked user.
The native exchange returns access and refresh tokens, persists one linked user and one session, and a replay answers 400 without a second user or session.
A wrong PKCE verifier on a native flow follows the web failure branch (302 Error in callback), creates no user or session and consumes the flow.
POST /logout for a web OIDC session returns the provider end-session URL with id_token_hint and the origin+base-path login redirect, expires the three cookies, deletes the session and keeps the user.
A web flow started before other /status and /ping requests still completes into a signed-in redirect.
Using a consumed mobile state or one the server never held answers 400 without a Location, credentials or state change.
After PATCH openid-unlink clears the subject and /api/me reports no link, the next email-matched login relinks the same user and adds one session.

A valid web callback redirects to the auth_cb URL with setToken/accessToken and no state, sets the refresh and Secure SameSite=Strict openid_id_token cookies, links the subject to one active user, creates one matching session and the access token authenticates /api/me.

Broken-signature, foreign-issuer, foreign-audience and expired ID tokens each answer 302 /login?error=Unauthorized&autoLaunch=0, leave users and sessions unchanged and consume the flow so a replay answers No sign-in session.
A provider access_denied and a state mismatch answer 302 Unauthorized, and a token-endpoint rejection answers 302 Error in callback; none creates a user or session.
Replaying a consumed web callback answers 302 /login?error=No sign-in session&autoLaunch=0 and creates no additional user or session.

Without a browser session an absent or empty code_verifier takes the web branch (302 No sign-in session) while a non-empty, repeated or openid-mobile-cookie request answers 400 without a user/session change.
A started web flow still completes after the same browser makes other /status requests.
A subject linked to a user deactivated after the start answers 302 Unauthorized, creates no session and leaves the users rows and newest updatedAt unchanged.

The native callback with the app's verifier answers 200 with the login payload (tokens, active linked user, default permissions, Source docker, first library, server settings, ereaderDevices), forwards the verifier and mobile redirect_uri to the token endpoint, and persists one session holding the returned refresh token that refreshes.
Repeating the native callback with the consumed session answers 400 without a second user or session.
An admin GET /auth/openid/config?issuer=<provider> answers 200 with exactly the seven forwarded discovery fields and does not forward code_challenge_methods_supported.
The discovery route answers 401 anonymously, 403 to a non-admin, and 400 for a missing, unparseable or unreachable issuer without leaking provider settings or internal errors.
A trailing slash on the issuer is stripped and the discovery document is fetched; a 404 document and an issuer carrying a query answer 400 without provider content.
The app's four native calls end in a 200 login payload whose access and refresh tokens authenticate, with one linked user and one session.
A wrong PKCE verifier takes the upstream web failure branch (302 Error in callback), creates no user or session and consumes the flow.
A native start without code_challenge_method is accepted, the provider URL states S256 and the flow completes with the matching verifier.
An empty or repeated code_verifier on a started native flow is rejected with 302 Error in callback and creates no user or session.
A second native login for the same subject reuses the user row (same id, type and extraData) and creates a second refreshable session.
With a group claim configured the scope includes it, groups=[admin] makes the user an admin and a later groups=[user] login downgrades it while both create sessions.
A missing group claim and a group outside admin/user/guest are denied with the login redirect and create no user or session.
A root user matched by email is denied for groups=[user] without a session or type change, succeeds unchanged for groups=[admin], and the temporary link can be cleared.
A non-admin login with the advanced-permissions claim persists the two false permissions on the linked user, leaves other defaults unchanged and reports them through GET /api/me.
A missing advanced-permissions claim is denied with the login redirect and the just auto-registered user is removed with no session left.
An email-matched admin keeps its permissions when the advanced-permissions claim would change them and the login succeeds with one session.
Removing openid from authActiveAuthMethods makes /status advertise only local; re-adding it advertises both and a complete web login succeeds.
OpenID settings persist across a restart, /status still advertises openid, and the boot-initialised strategy completes a web login.
Without the auth_cb cookie a valid web callback still creates the linked user and one session, sets the refresh cookie and answers 302 /login?error=No callback or already expired&autoLaunch=0.
Without a configured logout URL POST /logout answers 200 {redirect_url:null}, deletes the session and keeps the user.
The provider callback to /auth/openid/mobile-redirect answers 302 to the allowlisted app URI with the provider code and the started state, and that state cannot be used twice.
A consumed mobile state answers 400 without a Location or user/session change, while the callback that received the first answer still completes into one session.
A missing, empty, never-issued or web-flow state is rejected with 400 without a Location, credentials or user/session change.
A state the server does not hold (never issued or aged out) answers 400 without a Location, credentials or state change.
With two allowlisted app URIs a start for the second one forwards the provider result to that URI and its callback completes.
After a mobile state is consumed, a new start and redirect complete with a different state and its own code.
On a server with unconfigured OpenID settings GET /auth/openid answers an error status without a Location, auth cookies, token material or a user/session change.

A web start answers 302 to the configured provider with client_id, code response type, scope, random state, S256 challenge and the origin-based callback redirect_uri, sets HttpOnly auth_cb (600) and auth_method=openid (315360000) cookies plus a session, and returns no token material.

A native start for an allowlisted app URI and S256 challenge answers 302 carrying the app's challenge and the server's /auth/openid/mobile-redirect redirect_uri, sets auth_method=openid-mobile, no auth_cb and no token material.

authOpenIDSubfolderForRedirectURLs is inserted verbatim into both provider redirect_uris, restoring the empty value restores origin-only URLs, and a malformed value answers an error without a Location or state change.
Two web starts produce different states and both callbacks sign in and create their own session row.
An unlisted redirect_uri, missing challenge, non-S256 method, non-code response_type or state on the web flow is rejected with 400 and no Location, auth cookie or state change.

A callback that is absent, cross-origin, protocol-relative, backslash-prefixed, percent-decoded to protocol-relative, unparsable or outside the router base path is rejected with 400 and no Location, auth_cb cookie or state change.

not_applicable.reason: confirmed: GET /auth/openid only reads callback, redirect_uri, response_type, code_challenge, code_challenge_method and state (Auth.js:218-249, OidcAuthStrategy.js:291-386); no force/override/refresh switch exists.
confirmed: handleMobileRedirect only reads state and code and has no force/override mode (OidcAuthStrategy.js:483-510).
confirmed: the callback has no force/override parameter; behaviour is selected by the express session, code_verifier and the auth_method cookie (Auth.js:383-455).
confirmed: no mapped OIDC start, mobile-redirect, callback or code-exchange operation has a force, override or refresh mode.
confirmed: no OIDC route or strategy method implements a force/hard/override/refresh mode (Auth.js:362-523, OidcAuthStrategy.js).

open_findings: route-r003 record: cap-route-r003.json INV-R003-MOBILE-REPLAY-001 still carries the exception "The body text is asserted because it is the only client-visible denial besides the status; no client parses it.", but mobile-redirect-replay-400-changes-nothing no longer asserts a body and the contract no longer names one. Delete or rewrite the stale exception so the record does not claim an out-of-contract assertion.
